subject: Urgent: Customer performance incident — forensic evidence & legal hold
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <ops@brightledger.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — immediate help needed

Hi Priya / Rishi,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and elevated 5xx rates on our live endpoints around 08:50 PDT this morning. Throughput is roughly the same but tail latency has jumped to ~1.2s p95 (previously ~220ms) and overall error rate to ~4.6% (normal < 0.2%). This is impacting 3 of our high-traffic routes and tripping client-side retries.

We need two things urgently for our upcoming SOC audit and an internal board call: (1) a preserved snapshot of request logs, token/session identifiers, and any cache eviction events for 08:45–09:30 PDT, and (2) confirmation of what data is stored in the debug logs (any PII/PI, truncated vs full payloads).

Please advise what you can preserve now (and how to get it to us), and whether Redwood needs permission to keep any artifacts for >90 days under legal hold. We may need a formal legal hold letter if that is required.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure, BrightLedger
ops@brightledger.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the screenshot. I’m escalating to engineering and security now. Quick summary of next steps from my side:

- I’ve opened an internal incident (see PagerDuty link below) and asked eng to collect logs and KV cache artifacts for 08:40–09:35 PDT.
- Can you confirm the exact endpoints (route names) impacted? That will help scope the export.
- We can provisionally preserve artifacts for 90 days; if BrightLedger requests longer hold we’ll coordinate with Legal. Please send any formal hold language if you have it.

I’ve looped in Evelyn (security/compliance) and David (ops/forensics) to coordinate the evidence bundle and chain-of-custody. We’ll provide a manifest of exported files and a secure transfer link. ETA for an initial bundle: ~3–4 hours.

—Priya

Subject: Fwd: Production errors & latency spike — immediate help needed

Folks — forwarding Alex’s note. Requested items (priority order):

1) Raw request logs for customer routes (08:40–09:35 PDT) including request IDs, model variant, response codes, token counts, and any internal error stack traces.
2) KV cache eviction events and cache hit/miss rates for same window.
3) Runtime metrics: GPU queue depth, batching sizes, and per-worker error logs.
4) Authentication/access audit for any administrative access during the window (who pulled logs, who ssh’d into nodes).

We need to collect these under an evidence-preservation workflow (md5 checksums, timestamped archive, access ACLs) — David, can you take lead on packaging? Evelyn — please confirm any redaction policy we should apply before sharing with BrightLedger (PII/PI removal vs token truncation).

Thanks, Rishi

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <ops@brightledger.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 13:14:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — immediate help needed

Alex / team — I’m on this. High-level items and constraints from Security & Compliance: 

1) Evidence we can provide by EOD (preservation started at 10:02 PDT):
   - redwood_log_manifest_20270403.csv (CSV manifest with file paths, md5, and time ranges)
   - per-route request logs (redacted for user-submitted PII by default). Redaction policy: we strip fields designated as PII in our data-class map (emails, payment tokens). Full request IDs and internal tracing IDs will remain.
   - kv_cache_snapshot_20270403.tar.gz (cache metadata + eviction events; payloads excluded unless required and signed-off)
   - runtime metric dump (GPU queue depths, worker error counters, batching summary).

2) Access controls / chain of custody: any artifact export will be archived to a secure S3 bucket with restricted ACL, audit logging enabled, and access granted on an as-requested basis. We produce SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest.

3) Retention/legal hold: Redwood can implement a 180-day hold for this incident if BrightLedger sends an approval email or legal hold request. By default we retain 90 days. If BrightLedger needs us to retain artifacts longer, we’ll escalate to Legal for a contract addendum.

4) PII & token handling: our debug logs redact user-level PII. However, session/trace identifiers and truncated tokens (prefix/last-4 masked) are retained. If BrightLedger requires raw unredacted payloads for a regulatory subpoena, Legal will need to review and we will require an approved DPA amendment.

5) Next steps / ETA: David will post the initial manifest and an S3 transfer link by 14:30 PDT. We’ll include MD5/SHA256 checksums and a description of redaction applied. If BrightLedger confirms which routes they need full payloads for, we can start a separate review for unredacted exports.

I’ve attached a preservation checklist template and will follow up with the signed manifest.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
